overview: The committee reviewed proposed zoning boundaries and dimensional non-conformity data for the Boston Avenue corridor and discussed aligning the new regulations with the recently updated Medford Square zoning. The committee also considered the inclusion of private student housing and the jurisdictional reach of the Dover Amendment regarding institutional properties.

items.title: Call to Order and Presentation on Boston Avenue Corridor
items.summary: Chair Leming opened the meeting to continue discussions on the Boston Avenue corridor and the Tufts Institutional Zone. Emily Innes of Innes Land Strategies presented non-conformity studies demonstrating that the majority of existing buildings on Boston Avenue do not meet current zoning standards for frontage, setbacks, or lot size.

items.title: Discussion of Zoning Boundaries and Historical Development
items.summary: The committee discussed how historical development patterns predating modern zoning led to widespread non-conformity and the need for new regulations that permit reinvestment without requiring constant variances. Members suggested refining the corridor boundaries to include specific Apartment 1 districts and the St. Clement's Church property while excluding purely residential neighborhoods.

items.title: Private Student Housing and Sub-District Proposals
items.summary: Councilor Bears proposed including provisions for private, taxable student housing in the O2 zone to address the local housing shortage. Director of Planning Alicia Hunt noted that staff are investigating the complexities of such a use, including parking requirements and how to handle inclusionary housing.

items.title: Structural Alignment with Medford Square Zoning
items.summary: Staff and consultants discussed carrying over structural improvements and standardized definitions from the Medford Square zoning process to ensure citywide consistency. Director Hunt advised against using identical generic districts across different squares, arguing that each area requires tailored dimensional standards and incentives.

items.title: Public Comment and Tufts Institutional Zone Transparency
items.summary: Public commenters questioned the rationale for specific boundary changes and called for transparency regarding private meetings between the city and Tufts University. Chair Leming clarified that a list of Tufts' requested zoning points would be made public in a future council packet.

items.title: Legal Discussion on the Dover Amendment
items.summary: The committee received a briefing on the Dover Amendment, which exempts educational and religious institutions from certain zoning regulations only when the dominant use of the property serves a religious or educational mission.

items.title: Adjournment
items.summary: The committee kept the matter in committee and adjourned.
